messages.content: Analyze only the supplied record. Be precise and do not expose hidden reasoning.

You are reviewing a synthetic production incident. The service has four stages: client, gateway, scheduler, and model executor. At 09:00 traffic is 0.5 requests per second, concurrency is one, median prompt length is 80 tokens, TTFT is 0.42 seconds, output token rate is 28 tokens per second, errors are zero, and memory pressure is low. At 09:10 a batch client begins sending 3 requests per second with prompts between 1,600 and 2,200 tokens. Gateway validation remains below 3 milliseconds. The gateway permits 32 in-flight requests and has no explicit queue bound. Scheduler running requests rise from one to four and waiting requests rise from zero to twenty. TTFT P95 rises to 18 seconds, while time per output token changes from 36 to 39 milliseconds. CPU rises moderately, Metal utilization becomes bursty, and unified-memory pressure becomes yellow. At 09:12 the client retries every timeout immediately without jitter. Incoming traffic reaches 8 requests per second, timeout rate reaches 22 percent, and completed-request throughput declines. At 09:14 an operator increases the client timeout from 20 to 120 seconds. Timeout rate falls, but queue depth and P95 latency continue growing. At 09:17 the operator enables a gateway limit of four active upstream calls and a queue of eight, returning HTTP 429 with Retry-After when full. Queue depth stabilizes, completed throughput recovers, and TTFT P95 falls to 5.4 seconds. At 09:22 the batch client adds exponential backoff and jitter; TTFT P95 falls to 2.1 seconds. Repeated system prompts show a prefix-cache hit rate of 65 percent, but unique long prompts see no cache benefit. Output decoding remains between 25 and 28 tokens per second throughout. Produce: (1) a timeline, (2) the primary bottleneck and evidence, (3) contributing causes, (4) why the longer timeout did not fix capacity, (5) why bounded admission improved the system, (6) metrics and traces that distinguish prefill pressure from slow decoding, (7) two follow-up experiments, and (8) three alerts with cautious thresholds. Treat all numbers as synthetic input, not measurements from the current machine. Avoid recommending more hardware as the first action. Also explain how coordinated omission could make a load test look better than user experience and how the benchmark harness should avoid it. Discuss why retry storms are feedback loops. Explain the relationship among input length, prefill work, KV-cache allocation, queue residence time, TTFT, decode rate, and total latency. State which conclusions are directly supported and which remain hypotheses.
Analyze only the supplied specification. Be precise and do not expose hidden reasoning.

Create a production design review from this synthetic specification. A local language-model platform exposes an OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoint. Requests pass through a FastAPI gateway into a replaceable model backend. The gateway must reject malformed roles, empty messages, prompts beyond a configured token budget, negative generation limits, and unsupported sampling fields. It must propagate a request ID, enforce a queue wait timeout and an upstream deadline, cancel upstream work when the client disconnects, return an overload response when capacity is exhausted, and drain in-flight work during shutdown. The model process starts independently, pins model and tokenizer revisions, verifies artifact hashes, exposes readiness only after weights and KV cache are initialized, and never downloads a different revision during a benchmark. Operational metrics include request totals, active requests, queue depth, queue wait, TTFT, total latency, generated tokens, errors, timeouts, and cancellations. Labels must not contain prompt text, user IDs, request IDs, or unbounded exception messages. Structured logs include timestamp, severity, service, pipeline, request ID, event, duration, status, and safe error type. Infrastructure traces go to Tempo. LLM spans containing controlled benchmark prompt IDs, token counts, model identity, and evaluation attributes may go to Phoenix. Raw benchmark JSONL is authoritative. Each request records monotonic nanosecond timestamps, exact input and output token counts, stream event timestamps where valid, HTTP status, finish reason, and failure category. The experiment uses identical prompts, deterministic decoding, fixed warm-ups, concurrency one, two, and four, and a shared harness. Pipeline outputs may never share a directory. The comparison tool reads saved data only and must refuse mismatched protocol versions, base models, prompt hashes, generation settings, or tokenizer revisions. Review the design under these headings: data flow, lifecycle, overload behavior, streaming correctness, measurement validity, observability boundaries, privacy/cardinality, reproducibility, failure tests, and remaining risks. For each heading identify invariants, likely implementation mistakes, and an executable acceptance test. Explain which properties are genuinely exercised on one Apple-Silicon laptop and which claims would require a multi-node production environment. Do not invent performance results.
Analyze only the supplied experiment notes. Be precise and do not expose hidden reasoning.

A team plans to compare native BF16 and 4-bit versions of the same 1.7-billion-parameter language model on a 16 GB unified-memory computer. They propose the following flawed procedure: start both servers together; send different prompts to each; enable thinking only for the quantized model; use temperature 0.7 without fixed seeds; warm the first model for ten minutes but immediately measure the second; read P95 from two separate dashboard panels with different time ranges; omit failed requests from the raw files; calculate tokens per second using character count divided by time; let one run use a 2,048-token context and the other 8,192; update dependencies between runs; identify models only by mutable repository names; and ask a remote judge model to assign a single quality score without retaining judge prompts or separating objective tests. Rewrite this as a valid experimental protocol. Your answer must cover hypothesis, independent and controlled variables, artifact identity, tokenizer and chat-template identity, environment stabilization, sequential execution, workload construction, warm-up, concurrency, streaming timestamps, valid TTFT and inter-token measurements, token accounting, wall-clock aggregate throughput, error and timeout denominators, percentile population rules, memory baselines and peaks, model load timing, optional Metal sampling, raw schemas, file isolation, quality scoring, comparison preconditions, statistical limitations, and stop conditions for memory pressure. Include a section explaining why a smaller model may be required if BF16 is unsafe, and why both pipelines must then be resized together. Include another section explaining why the comparison program must never launch either model. Finish with a reproducibility checklist and a list of statements the final report must not make unless supported by saved evidence. Do not calculate or invent any benchmark values.
